newsitem.title: UK: BAe extends gain as U.S. merger seen positive.
newsitem.headline: BAe extends gain as U.S. merger seen positive.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace Plc extended Monday's late recovery on Tuesday amid hopes that the merger plan announced by Boeing and McDonnell Douglas would ultimately prove favourable for the UK group.
British Aerospace shares were up 17-1/2p at 11.54 stg by 1025 GMT.

"In the longer term the proposed merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas probably has to be a positive," said Lehman Brothers analyst Guy Kekwick, who repeated an "outperform" rating on BAe shares.
"It must give impetus and a sense of urgency to change Airbus which maybe was a bit lacking."
Plans to create a European aircraft enterprise out of the dragged on because of reluctance by some members to give up control of core development and production capabilities.

"It will be a complex transition which has had the luxury of time. Maybe now that luxury is no longer there," Kekwick said. He said the U.S. merger "...could act as catalyst for faster change in Airbus which in itself could be a positive for British Aerospace".
Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, BAe, Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA ) of Spain.
